title: LSP stdio initialize rootfs identity

environment.system_features: ACL GMP GNUTLS LIBSELINUX LIBXML2 MODULES NATIVE_COMP NOTIFY INOTIFY PDUMPER SECCOMP SQLITE3 THREADS TREE_SITTER ZLIB

mechanism: LSP task evidence must include the language-server process, protocol lifecycle, workspace root, and rootfs-owned executable path.
hypothesis: Batch-safe JSON-RPC initialize/shutdown exchanges should succeed for the production C/C++, Python, and Rust language servers that are present in the selected rootfs.
minimal_fixture: Temporary C++, Python, and Rust workspaces plus stdio JSON-RPC exchanges with clangd, pyright-langserver, and rust-analyzer.
predicted_behavior: Each production server should answer `initialize', accept `shutdown', receive `exit', and expose a rootfs-owned executable path.

independent_checks.name: LSP stdio initializer script ran in production
production LSP servers initialized and shut down
production LSP server executables are rootfs-owned

counterexample: A benchmark can pass via direct text mutation while the intended language server never starts, starts from the host, or cannot initialize against the workspace.
derived_gym_requirement: LSP benchmarks must record server executable identity, pid, workspace root, initialize response, shutdown status, and document-version evidence before trusting refactor results.
